# book_report

Show the book whose title the request names: its author and copies, and who has it on loan when asked. With brief, only whether the library has it.

Source: `_commands/book_report.py`.

Calls: `find_book`, `list_loans`, `show_book`.
Depth: 1 (lower bound; open steps name no command)

## Inputs

| input | type | default | sample | verify | in_request | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | str | required | `<title>` |  |  | the book's title |
| `loans` | bool | false | false |  |  | the request asks who has the book on loan |
| `brief` | bool | false | false |  |  | the request only asks whether the library has the book |

## Example requests

- tell me about Dune and who has it
- do you have Emma at all

## Phases

| phase | output | runs | fans out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `find` | `Found` | always | no |
| `book` | `Book` | only when brief = false, and then only when `find.book_uids` | no |
| `loans` | `Loans` | only when loans = true, brief = false | no |

## Answer

### Answer when loans = false, brief = false

Written by `__result__`: \<book.name> is by \<book.author>; the library owns \<book.copies> copies.

### Answer when brief = true

Written by `__result__`: Yes, the library has \<title>.

### Answer when loans = true, brief = false

Written by `__result__`: \<book.name> is by \<book.author>; the library owns \<book.copies> copies. It is on loan to \<loans.total> borrower (\<loans.borrowers[0]>).
